rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.sdk.outlines.Span`.

**Index<Span> for str** (`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[span_indexes_str_at_utf8_byte_boundaries]`)
- It uses the source "aé🦀" with spans (0,0), (1,3) and (3,7), and asserts `&source[span] == &source[span.start..span.end]`.
- It asserts exact slices: (1,3) gives "é" and the empty span at the end, (7,7), gives "". This covers the inclusive start and exclusive end.
- It asserts a panic for each invalid span:
  - Spans (2,3), (0,2) and (2,2) have offsets inside a multi-byte character.
  - Span (0,8) has an end past `source.len()`.
  - Span (3,1) has `start > end`.
- These are the failure cases in the validity rule `start <= end <= len` plus the UTF-8 boundary rule, which the requirement says must match the checks of the range index.

**Trait implementations**
- `needs_eq::<Span>()` checks `Eq`.
- `Copy` and `Clone` follow from using `span` by value in `&source[span]` and then reading `span.start` and `span.end`. The type also derives `Clone` and `Copy`.
- `Debug` and `PartialEq` are exercised by `assert_eq!` on `Span` values in `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` and `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans`.

**Byte offsets from the original snapshot, including nested items**
- `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` checks that real outline spans are byte offsets, not char offsets. For source "é\n \t\n🦀\n" it expects (0,len), (0,2) and (6,10), and that `&source[item.span]` equals the item text.
- `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans` covers nested items inside a directive, a quote and a list, with non-ASCII text. It asserts `item.span.start` and `name_span` are offsets in the whole original source. It also asserts `selected.text() == &source[item.span]`.

**`#[non_exhaustive]` and the public shape**
- The `compile_fail,E0639` doctest on `Span` checks that a struct literal is rejected.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the export inventory.

I found no uncovered obligation. Other out-of-range inputs, such as `start` greater than `len`, fall in the same invalid-bounds class as the tested cases.

text: `trust_but_verify::outline::Span` locates text by byte offsets from the start
of the original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item.
`start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive. A valid span satisfies
`start <= end <= source.len()` and both offsets are UTF-8 character boundaries.
For `source: &str`, `&source[span]` yields the same slice as
`&source[span.start..span.end]`, with the same bounds and boundary checks.
pub fn new(start: usize, end: usize) -> Self;
